# NOTES ON TWO BOOKS (Robert Barr & Harold Bindloss)

## BOOK 1 of 2: LORD STRANLEIGH ABROAD (Robert Barr, 1913, Ward, Locke & Co.; Gutenberg 32185)
Frontispiece: "'Why did you wish to murder me?'" (p.189). Contents: I Lord Stranleigh All at Sea (p7); II An Automobile Ride (49); III The God in the Car (87); IV The Mad Miss Maturin (125); V In Search of Game (164); VI The Bunk House Prisoner (209); VII The End of the Contest (259).

**Main characters:** Lord Stranleigh (Earl of Stranleigh of Wychwood; alias Edmund Trevelyan, then Henry Johnson, then "Henry Johnson" chauffeur, then "Edmund Stranleigh" at ranch; shy, indolent, wealthy, lucky "by flukes," rarely thinks; dresses well). Ponderby (his valet; dislikes America, "born a servant"; blushes; Londoner; given $15,000 in Altonville bank as "Ponderby" enacting country gentleman). Hon. John "Jack" Hazel (ex-Camperdown Club gambler, expelled; travels third-class; Stranleigh gets him cabin 4390; William Jones = steerage name; promises not to gamble). Ned Trenton (Philadelphia coal/railway man; host of Pennsylvania estate; Stranleigh's friend; ex-Stranleigh guest in England). Mrs. Vanderveldt (Trenton's sister, Sis; husband dreamy ex-Minister to Italy). Constance Maturin (Miss Maturin; heiress; "conservation" dams; model city on heights above Powerville; mad per Boscombe). John L. Boscombe (millionaire, Powerville co-owner; opposes Maturin). Wentworth Parkes (ex-valet of Duke of Rattleborough, forger of letter; wants $100,000 for Sterling Motor option; Detroit). J.E. Sterling (young engineer, Woodbridge Street, Detroit; safety pegs on car). Branksome Poole / Charles Branksome (gambler/blackmailer; alias husband of Mrs. Poole). Mrs. Branksome Poole (unnamed; was Miss Trevelyan; daughter of wealthy father; English; married in America; ill-treated; told Stranleigh; got £100). Dr. (ship surgeon, friend). Erasmus Blank (millionaire blackmail target). Stanmore Anson (old Swedish-descended mill-owner, Anson's Mill, Altonville, Ohio/NY-type valley; opposes G.K.R. Trust); Gertrude Anson Challis (his daughter; married Jim Challis, engineer at Fulmer's grist mill, Altonville); Mrs. Anson. Asa Perkins (Boston; owns house). Langdon, Bliss & Co. (firm employing Challis). Duke of Rattleborough (cabled Parkes is forger). Mr. Banks (John L. Banks, Ice Trust attorney; gives letter to Stanley Armstrong). Stanley Armstrong (rancher, mining/silver; ranch near Bleachers; Chicago trip; "Armstrong's ranch"). Miss Armstrong ("Professor"; doctor, Lausanne-trained, cooking school at Thun; "Madame Curie" ambition; charges in francs/dollars). Jim Dean (leader of six bunk house men; shot Stranleigh in left shoulder; "Dean"; ear shot by Stranleigh; handkerchief with crest). Silas A. Ricketts (Bleachers lawyer; holds $5,000 note; $5 per hour; sheriff in his pocket). Timmins (other lawyer). Detective Burns (NY; Pinkerton telegram). Peter (hand). Sheriff (auctioneer). Old Mrs. Armstrong.

**Events in order (Book 1):**
- Ch I: Stranleigh boards at Southampton; Ponderby; Dr. (ship surgeon) greets him; Hazel met; Stranleigh buys Hazel's cabin 4390 from purser ($50 notes, £100 total for girl later); Hazel's cabin; Mrs. Branksome Poole (Miss Trevelyan) asks; Stranleigh gives her £100 (two £50 notes, numbers differ by one). Poole visits Stranleigh's suite demanding money; Ponderby throws him out. Mrs. Poole in Ponderby's room; plan: wireless detention. Hazel cheats Poole at poker on ship (two £50 notes retrieved); Poole exposed; wireless; arrested in NY.
- Ch II: Stranleigh travels under names; Parkes (Wentworth) pursues with Sterling Motor option; Stranleigh tests car; cable to Rattleborough ("Letter a forgery. Parkes was my valet..."). Stranleigh goes to Canada (St. John), then Detroit as "Henry Johnson." Meets Sterling in Woodbridge Street shop; safety pegs (centre stops engine, right/left steer). Stranleigh gives Sterling $500 for week's option; Parkes becomes chauffeur, tries blackmail ($100,000) on Canadian shore; Stranleigh throws him into river. Stranleigh pays Parkes via Sterling ($500 + $500).
- Ch III: Stranleigh as "Henry Johnson" chauffeur; Ponderby as gentleman; Burford/Lenthall butler story; Ponderby gets $15,000 in Altonville bank. Stranleigh drives to lakes; meets young Challis (Jim) and wife Gertrude (sprained ankle); takes them home; Challis tells story (Anson mill; Langdon Bliss; Anson's letter "wolf in sheep's clothing"). Anson's mill sold at auction Nov 17; Stranleigh buys mill and 10 acres for Anson's price; Anson insists on naming manager; Challis appointed; Gertrude reconciled ("Shall we throw our differences on that scrap-heap?").
- Ch IV: Edward (Ned) Trenton host; Maturin dams; Mrs. Vanderveldt ("Sis"); Miss Maturin's car ride (six-cylinder); Stranleigh offers capital; Boscombe warns ("stark mad"); Stranleigh buys nothing; Powerville celebration; dam bursts ("This is murder!"; Stranleigh: "Whoever is responsible ... should be hanged!").
- Ch V: Stranleigh at University Club with Banks (Ice Trust); Banks recommends Stanley Armstrong's ranch. Stranleigh travels by rail to Bleachers; mules, guide; shot in left shoulder at edge of ranch; guide and escort abandon him; Stranleigh holds up hands/pantomime; reaches house; Mrs. Armstrong and Miss Armstrong (doctor) treat wound; Jim Dean's shot "to nip"; Miss Armstrong explains father's debt to Ricketts ($5,000); Stranleigh offers $3,000 loan (total $5,500 with Timmins).
- Ch VI: Stranleigh explores silver mine; men (Jim and five) warn him off with rifles; dynamite in mine; Stranleigh rides to Bleachers (red shotgun "imaginary line"); visits Ricketts ($5 for an hour); telegraph operator (Western Union, "Pinkerton Detective Agency, Chicago," $100 reward, twenty thousand dollars express from NY); operator reports to Ricketts; Stranleigh captured at dusk by Jim and five; bunk house prisoner; Jim's demand: pay $ for ranch.
- Ch VII: Stranleigh escapes by chimney, sooty; wires dynamite into wall; shoots Jim's left ear (handkerchief with crest); armistice; Stranleigh pays bunk men $50 each for bodyguard; meets Armstrong on road, buys ranch at auction (Agricultural Hall, Bleachers) for $17,000 (bids vs Ricketts' $16,000; sheriff); deeds ranch to Miss Armstrong as "medical bill" + Jim's bill; "Lord Stranleigh of Wychwood" — crest and monogram exposed; Miss Armstrong: "Good-bye to you, Lord Stranleigh of Wychwood."

## BOOK 2 of 2: THE IMPOSTOR (Harold Bindloss, Ward, Lock & Co.; Gutenberg 39698)
Frontispiece: "In the meanwhile, Maud Barrington sat by the open window in her room." (Ch XVI). Chapters: I Rancher Witham; II Lance Courthorne; III Trooper Shannon's Quarrel; IV In the Bluff; V Miss Barrington Comes Home; VI Anticipations; VII Witham's Decision; VIII Witham Comes to Silverdale; IX An Armistice; X Maud Barrington's Promise; XI Speed the Plough; XII Mastery Recognized; XIII A Fair Advocate; XIV The Unexpected; XV Facing the Flame; XVI Maud Barrington is Merciless; XVII With the Stream; XVIII Under Test; XIX Courthorne Blunders; XX The Face at the Window; XXI Colonel Barrington is Convinced; XXII Sergeant Stimson Confirms his Suspicions; XXIII The Revelation; XXIV Courthorne makes Reparation; XXV Witham Rides Away; XXVI Reinstation.

**Main characters:** Rancher (Frank/F.) Witham (Englishman, ~26, grey eyes, bronzed, ruined by blizzard, mortgage foreclosure; hotel girl Nettie; ruined; horses killed by Witham). Lance Courthorne (gambler, whisky-runner, English aristocrat, blue eyes, black horse; disinherited; son of Geoffrey Courthorne; deal: Witham rides his black to draw police; $100 paid). Trooper Pat Shannon (Irish, Ontario bush; loves Ailly Blake; Courthorne whipped him; killed by Courthorne in bluff; last word "Witham"). Trooper Payne (English, later Corporal; friend of Shannon). Sergeant Stimson (grizzled; police). Larry Blake (Ailly's brother). Colonel Barrington (founder/ruler of Silverdale Grange, English settlement; Geoffrey's old friend; hates Courthorne). Miss Barrington (his sister; silver-haired, gentle; knew Lance's mother). Maud Barrington (niece; ward; Montreal; brown eyes; "Princess of the Prairie"; holds Silverdale land; Twoinette friend). Gordon Dane (big bronzed bachelor, lieutenant). Graham (Winnipeg wheat-broker). Macdonald (farmer; wife). Alfreton (young lad; speculator). Ferris (Silverdale lad; gambler; set fire; expelled). Hassal, Allardyce, Stapleton, Atterly, Carshalton, Jake, Tom (hired hands). Mrs. Carndall (gossip). Colonel's wife absent. Lily (girl with Atterly). Mrs. Jasper (hotel). Nettie (hotel-keeper's daughter). Sergeant Stimson; trooper Bacon; trooper Hilton; Jackson; Harland (magistrate); Doctor (unnamed).

**Events (Book 2):**
- Ch I: Witham at Canadian settlement (prairie, Alberta/Canada); mail: foreclosure letter; wagon accident; horses lost; he kills one horse with knife.
- Ch II: Courthorne at Witham's house; offer $100 to ride black along Montana trail; Witham agrees; Courthorne lies about risk.
- Ch III: Courthorne's black; Witham rides away; trooper Shannon and Payne sent by Stimson to watch Graham's Pool; Shannon's quarrel story; Witham rides, chase, escapes over bridge.
- Ch IV: Bluff at river; Shannon confronts Courthorne; Courthorne shoots Shannon twice; Courthorne rides into river; Payne sees Courthorne sink; Shannon dies saying "Witham."; Sergeant Stimson injured by horse fall; Witham's Marlin rifle left.
- Ch V: Maud Barrington returns from Montreal; Colonel Barrington, Silverdale; Courthorne history (dog hanged, gardener's boy lied).
- Ch VI: Maud and aunt talk; Colonel and Dane; wheat selling forward; Graham advice refused.
- Ch VII: Witham arrested as "Courthorne" at outpost; learns Shannon killed and "Witham" presumed drowned; lawyer at Annerly; Witham takes Courthorne's identity to Silverdale.
- Ch VIII: Witham arrives at Silverdale dinner (black coat, deerskin); Dane's support; whist/poker quarrel; Maud's contempt.
- Ch IX: Blizzard; Witham and Maud in shanty; Witham sacrifices to keep her warm; they sleep; Witham leaves at dawn.
- Ch X: Witham reports to Colonel; Maud's promise (sow wheat, not sell forward).
- Ch XI: Ploughing, Witham's own land; Miss Barrington's blessing "God speed your plough"; Witham pays Maud.
- Ch XII: Gambler (Ferris's card game in saloon); Witham exposes; Ferris blackmailed; trooper Payne sees.
- Ch XIII: Maud defends Witham before neighbours; Maud & Witham in buggy in moonlight.
- Ch XIV: Harvest; Witham's bargain with Maud (use of land); Courthorne appears at homestead (wanted money); Witham agrees to pay $1,000 + 2nd thousand.
- Ch XV: Grass fire; Witham's quick ploughing; Dane leads; Witham badly hurt; carried to Grange.
- Ch XVI: Witham recovering; Ferris expelled by Dane; Maud forbids Witham to probe fire.
- Ch XVII: Wheat prices; Witham to Winnipeg; Graham; wheat up; Alfreton covered; Witham makes profit; supper.
- Ch XVIII: Bridge (Witham builds); Maud crosses at night; Courthorne appears; attacks; plank gap; Witham saves Courthorne; Courthorne threatens over Maud; Witham tells him to stay away.
- Ch XIX: Courthorne blunders (saloon, girl, decanter); trooper Bacon papers; Stimson & Payne consult; Guyler; Witham fights stranger; Colonel sees Witham ejecting man; Colonel suspicious.
- Ch XX: Stimson and Payne ride; Payne visits Courthorne's homestead; Dane's talk; party at Grange; Maud's "play" parallel; face at window; Courthorne collapses.
- Ch XXI: Courthorne at Witham's homestead; confesses shooting Shannon; given $500; goes to Chicago; Witham offers Colonel $contract help; Colonel's wheat short; Witham's I.O.U to Maud.
- Ch XXII: Harvest; Stimson in Alberta arrests Harmon's helper; message "Send me five hundred dollars."
- Ch XXIII: Harvest done; wheat sold; Witham's revelation at harvest dinner; Stimson's warrant; Courthorne flees; Payne issues warrant; Courthorne escapes.
- Ch XXIV: Witham statement; $1,000 claim; Stimson arrests Witham; Courthorne's deposition (shot Shannon; Witham unknowing); Courthorne rides at troopers, shot by Payne, dies; Colonel gets sick.
- Ch XXV: Witham leaves Silverdale; Maud and Witham parting; Witham to Graham's Winnipeg; partner; St. Louis mills; 30,000 dollars; flour orders.
- Ch XXVI: Year later; Colonel's sleigh accident; Witham returns; proposal to Maud; wedding; Maud: "There never was a Courthorne who could stand beside him." London: Ward, Lock & Co.
